method: web open and read public primary HTML

entries.author: Trinity College London editorial collection; named teacher contributions by Lucinda Adams, John Ennis and Irita Kutchmy
entries.title: The Teacher’s Guide to Musicianship & Technical Exercises
entries.edition: Public HTML; individual page publication date and editorial byline not stated; linked 2021–2023 resources are not the page date
entries.section: Encouraging Improvisation; Give both hands Focus
entries.evidence: Adams recommends early call and response. Ennis restricts the initial note set and uses a target note reached by different routes. Kutchmy starts with two or three notes. The separate-hands section recommends gradual preparation before combining hands.
entries.application: One prepared RH creative answer with a limited three-note set, an ending on C4 and two genuinely different answers; later changed-question transfer stays outside automatic grading.
entries.limits: Teacher recommendations, not experimental evidence, approval of this course or an examined performance. CDE register,123 fingers,48BPM,4+4+4 beats and practice criteria are project choices. No famous-pupil claim, video or PDF specimen inspected.

entries.author: Trinity College London; individual byline not stated
entries.title: Piano improvisation specimen tests
entries.edition: Public HTML; individual publication date not stated; footer copyright is not the publication date
entries.evidence: The motivic option asks for solo improvisation in response to a short melodic fragment.
entries.application: Distinguish a learner-created response from reproducing the fixed listening example.
entries.limits: Context only; not the Trinity exam, equivalent level, copied specimen, unseen ear test or automated judgment. Linked PDF, audio and video specimens were not inspected.
